limits: Python processes only: a child that is not Python (git, sh) runs code nobody sees (children.other)

a child Python process is seen only when it inherits PYTHONPATH and runs without -I, -E, -S: a test that builds its own env= starts a child this recorder cannot see (children.unhooked_python), and so does a child of one; a child launched with no subprocess.Popen/os.posix_spawn/os.spawn/os.system audit event is not counted either way

not matched: C-level calls, code with no file (exec, compile, dataclass-generated methods), and product code run from a copy of the tree whose file name or path tail differs; a copy with the tree's name, path tail and bytes is counted (executed_from_copy_only), one with other bytes is another version (other_version), not counted
a hit is lost when the process has no free file descriptor at that moment (retried at the next call)
a function executed before the hook is installed (the interpreter start) is not seen: none of the watched ones can be
'executed' says the function's code object started; not a line, a branch, or that its result was used

one-sided: a function WAS executed in the kill files and children measured; never that one was NOT executed outside the children hooked. A target whose kill files ran none of the watched functions and loaded no file whose module statements changed has no changed code in its measured behaviour
module-level statements are not functions: `loaded` is the import; `module_statements_executed` is the import of a file whose module statements (or class bodies) are new or changed
the unmutated tree: a mutant may execute what the original does not
scope: aisef2/**.py and validation/v2/cleanup_authority.py; other changed files of the runner's tree are in diff.outside_scope; data files, environment and timing are not code
a kill file that READS the source of a changed file (an AST scan, a grep invariant, a hash) executes none of it: that is read_set.py's `opened`; a consumer needs both records
a def adds a name to its module's namespace: visible without running the function only to code that enumerates it (dir, inspect.getmembers); not an import-time statement here
the environment differs from the runner's by PYTHONPATH (and sys.path with it): a test that asserts on either fails here and is recorded as not passed
measured on POSIX (macOS, Linux); Windows is not exercised

a.what: a watched function called in the test process is recorded

b.what: a module imported with none of its watched functions called is NOT executed (it is loaded)

c.what: a watched function called only in a child Python process that inherits PYTHONPATH is recorded

d.what: called in a child with its own env= is NOT recorded, and the child is counted unhooked_python

e.what: a watched function called from a thread is recorded

f.what: a process SIGKILLed right after the call has recorded it

g.what: the recorder changes no kill file's PASS/FAIL (a passing and a failing toy, hooked and plain)

h.what: the qualified names this tool derives from the AST are the ones the interpreter reports

i.what: a forked child records its own first hit although its parent's first hit disabled the event

j.what: product code run from a byte-identical copy of the tree is recorded (flagged); another version is not

k.what: descriptors the code under test closes do not lose later hits (the recorder holds no descriptor)
